stage_2_story.text_en: Roni had been trying to reach his father Shimon all morning. When he finally picked up, Shimon sounded half asleep. 'Dad, it's eleven o'clock,' Roni said. 'I know,' Shimon replied. 'I hit the sack late — your mother and I stayed up arguing about the renovation again.' Roni sighed. He drove over, and the moment he walked in, he could tell his parents were still not seeing eye to eye about the kitchen. His mother wanted to knock down a wall; his father thought that was absurd. Roni poured himself a coffee and sat down. His mother immediately launched into her reasons — but she was beating around the bush for so long that Roni finally said, 'Mum, I love you, but just tell me what you actually want.' She laughed and admitted she had always dreamed of an open-plan kitchen. His father crossed his arms. 'I'll believe the builder's timeline when I take it with a grain of salt,' he muttered. He had once hired a contractor who had promised three weeks and taken three months. Roni tried to help. He suggested they hire a designer and at least look at some plans. Shimon wasn't ready to decide. He was still on the fence. 'Don't jump on the bandwagon just because the neighbours redid their kitchen,' he said to his wife. She shook her head. 'This isn't a trend. This is our home.' Roni could see the argument was beginning to get out of hand, so he stepped in. 'Listen,' he said carefully. 'Don't either of you throw the other under the bus here. You're on the same side.' That calmed things down. They agreed to visit a showroom together that weekend. As Roni left, he smiled to himself. He had come to fix a lightbulb and ended up mediating a family peace deal. He hoped he hadn't bitten off more than he could chew — because he was pretty sure they'd ask him to manage the whole renovation.
